nodes.label: Stack Moko Baby — functional specification
nodes.rationale: Confirmed/current Matrix integration supersedes older Classic-only proposals below. The specification distinguishes implemented software, proposed requirements and measured acceptance.

nodes.label: Boot bound recovery extends uncertain state workflow
nodes.rationale: Connectivity loss does not stop an authorized local round. Unknown start/reboot retains a review lock; only matching durable evidence and guarded current-boot stop receipts permit resolution. Incomplete traces never earn points; no-score closure expires the ticket and reentry needs a scan.

nodes.label: Historical Classic v1 scoring and deterministic timing
nodes.rationale: Historical Classic v1 baseline uses 8 columns/12 rows, three-cell support, integer bounce, 100 points per successful row plus 25 perfect bonus, maximum 1,500. Movement precedes placement at equal timestamps and timeout wins at 60,000 ms. Current new assignments use Matrix v1; historical Classic results retain their rules.

nodes.label: Confirmed LED matrix button game with device timing authority
nodes.rationale: ESP32 owns local movement, button input, countdown, timeout and feedback. Server authorizes ranked assignments, retains immutable rules and replays evidence. Browsers cannot author ranked scores or bypass physical readiness.

nodes.label: Pooled overlap accuracy with N A for absent attempts
nodes.rationale: Accuracy is 100*sum(overlap)/sum(candidate widths), includes recorded zero-overlap attempts, and is null without attempts. Timeout creates no invented failed row. This is a game-derived ratio, not a physical sensor or skill measurement.

nodes.label: Private scan registration and one live ticket per player
nodes.rationale: QR holds event/machine URL only. Required student ID is identification, not authentication: preserve leading zeros; a new browser cannot acquire an existing player's ticket by knowing the ID. Private entry grant/session and one live ticket per event are enforced; operator recovery remains an operational gate.

nodes.label: Role separation and release thresholds are requirements
nodes.rationale: Visitor/player/operator/admin/device/AI access is specified, not proof that distinct staff permissions are complete. Targets include 20 concurrent assignments, exactly-once terminal replay, 2-second LAN leaderboard p95, 50-ms hardware input p95, 500-ms LAN API p95 at 50 clients, accessibility, isolated restore and 50 cabinet rounds plus two-hour soak; unrun gates stay open.

nodes.label: Selected Matrix v1 supersedes Classic-only proposals
nodes.rationale: Current assignments use the selected sketch's 16 columns, 15 levels, six-cell starting support, one point per placement and no bonus; Classic history stays unchanged. No remote browser play is requested. Wokwi first, physical timing/power/difficulty acceptance later; Render AI connection is deferred.

nodes.label: Cabinet state lifecycle, offline play and terminal persistence
nodes.rationale: BOOT/SELF_TEST/IDLE/RESERVED/COUNTDOWN/PLAYING/RESULT_PENDING plus fault/maintenance describe observations; persisted server session is authoritative. Pre-assignment button cannot start ranked play. Offline authorized round may continue, but no offline new assignment; persist start/terminal before success and retain review/terminal locks across stale heartbeat/reboot/corrupt storage.

nodes.label: Best-game ranking, source/ruleset cohorts and local dates
nodes.rationale: Rank each player's best valid completed round by score, completed level, duration, completion time and session ID. Separate source/ruleset cohorts, exclude aborted/expired/review/practice/invalidated results, use Asia/Manila day bounds, and label stale live observations without fictitious animation.

nodes.label: Pending physical, identity and network release decisions
nodes.rationale: Confirm actual ESP32/panels/pins/power/current budget, approved ID format/recovery owner, tested difficulty/absence timeout, event LAN/hostname/certificate trust, AI policy/budget and institution-approved retention. Baseline retention durations remain proposals rather than enacted policy.

nodes.label: Stack Moko Baby — MySQL data model
nodes.rationale: Ordered backend migrations are authoritative for running MariaDB 10.11.16; candidate schema.sql and historical Alembic advice are superseded. This reference covers immutable rules, transactional integrity, private identity and bounded operational/assistant data.

nodes.label: Backend versioned migrations override candidate DDL
nodes.rationale: Current ordered SQL migrations, including 005 recovery and 006 Matrix rules, govern implementation; schema.sql remains a candidate reference. Additive migrations preserve existing identities and result columns.

nodes.label: Committed event revisions and outbox hints
nodes.rationale: Relevant mutations increment global event revision and insert safe empty-payload outbox rows atomically; idempotent retries allocate no new revision. Dispatcher publication means queued, not browser-acknowledged. Current authorized repeatable-read snapshots supersede old payload/revision meanings.

nodes.label: Generated active machine and live player uniqueness
nodes.rationale: Generated stored active-machine key is unique across reserved/countdown/playing/awaiting-result/review; live-player key prevents duplicate waiting/assigned event tickets. Composite FKs bind event/player/machine/session; each ticket maps to at most one session. Review preserves the machine lock.

nodes.label: Identity encryption HMAC and proposed retention privacy
nodes.rationale: Institution-scoped HMAC lookup and separate authenticated encryption protect identity; public codes are unrelated labels. HMAC key rotation searches all active versions before insertion and needs staged tested rekeying. Proposed 30-day identity retention includes HMAC mappings and backup lifecycle; required ID does not prove ownership. Real records, keys, dumps and exports stay outside Graphify/model inputs.

nodes.label: Migration005 boot journal conflicts and command bindings
nodes.rationale: Migration 005 adds device_boots, immutable device_journal_events and conflict fingerprints; current boot, predecessor/storage epoch, monotonic event sequence and uptime are bound to commands/sessions. Quarantine disables unsafe recovery. No private identity column is introduced and raw operational rows cannot enter graph/model inputs.

nodes.label: Pooled overlap ratio and NULL missing denominator
nodes.rationale: Pooled overlap is sum(overlap)/sum(attempted width), rather than mean of percentages. Missing denominators produce N/A and timeouts create no placement. Best-game rankings use score, level, duration, completion time and session ID within event/ruleset/source; query integrity requires actual MariaDB checks.

nodes.label: Private typed memory and reviewed owner scoped datasets
nodes.rationale: Migrations 003/004 store staff-owned typed topics/preferences and reviewed normalized-input/routing labels. Forget uses an advancing tombstone revision; stale writes fail. Example approval/export checks ownership, revision and current context; quota is 1,000/admin with 25-row pages. No raw chat, answer prose or game values are stored.

nodes.label: UTC millisecond time canonical hash and transaction boundaries
nodes.rationale: UTC DATETIME(3), explicit connection timezone, half-open Asia/Manila-converted ranges and canonical validated payload hashes prevent ambiguity. Lock event→machine→queue→session, never hold transactions across network I/O. Result replay, placements, ticket, receipt and outbox commit before ACK; delayed observations cannot move completed state backward.

nodes.label: Migration 006 Matrix rules and authenticated command ordering
nodes.rationale: 006_matrix_rules.sql inserts immutable matrix-v1 and selects it through event settings without replacing identity/placement/score columns. Session ruleset ID/hash remains fixed through completion/recovery. Source/ruleset filters preserve Classic histories; command ID becomes authenticated monotonic deliverySequence for durable firmware rejection.

nodes.label: Immutable recovery evidence and atomic guarded closure
nodes.rationale: Recovery never rewrites original journal rows. Guarded release/void/full-trace recovery commits session/ticket/result, audit, receipt and live invalidation together. Public responses exclude boot/storage/receipt/journal data; uncertain sessions retain machine uniqueness until matching evidence or audited recovery.

nodes.label: Explicit current measures override history and contradictory model labels
nodes.rationale: Explicit current requested measures override prior history, demonstrations and contradictory schema-valid model labels. Inherit only omitted supported typed slots. Player-score paging returns best valid completed public-code scores per source, 50 rows/page, with bounded 1–2,000 page and continuation metadata.

nodes.label: Student identity raw questions and private values excluded from model context
nodes.rationale: Keep student IDs, lookup hashes, ciphertext, credentials, raw questions/history, nicknames, game rows and operational journals out of model context. Only reviewed vocabulary and validated typed hints reach routing. Safe metadata is separate from read-only game analytics; no prompt/answer retention by default.

nodes.label: Eight bounded allowlisted read-only analytics operations
nodes.rationale: Eight internal operations cover event summary, top scores, level statistics, play trend, machine summary, queue summary, distribution and paged player scores. Strict server-bound event/ruleset/window, caps and fixed SQL govern access; backend templates format every factual claim with current scope/evidence. Registration and completed-player denominators differ.

nodes.label: Analytics-v1 runtime and development AI system rules
nodes.rationale: Analytics-v1 defines runtime and development boundaries. Enforce authority/privacy/query validation in the backend, not solely prompts; current inference returns intent only and never writes factual prose.

nodes.label: AI cannot resolve device holds or issue operational commands
nodes.rationale: AI may explain approved recovery knowledge but cannot stop devices, resolve holds, mutate queue/results, manage identity or receive journal/storage/command secrets. Those actions belong to actual authenticated deterministic device/operator services with evidence/revision checks.

nodes.label: Public projection unresolved-subject guard and separate topical decision
nodes.rationale: Apply privacy/control checks before reviewed lexical projection. Unknown stripped subjects require clarification. Broader wording needs a separate topical decision that keywords cannot override; familiar explicit supported requests can bypass inference while retaining admin/enablement/rate/deadline/fresh-data protections.

nodes.label: Freeze cases labels runtime lexicon and scorer before unseen evaluation
nodes.rationale: Freeze cases/gold/runtime/prompt/corpus/lexicon/scorer before first-use inference. Use diverse 100–300+ cases and about 20–50/intent, count errors/valid clarifications, and report uncertainty. Keep holdouts outside retrieval/training/Graphify. Inspected reuse is regression, and weak larger-set results cannot be replaced by stronger visible probes.

nodes.label: Matrix-aware analytics and cloud AI disabled
nodes.rationale: Level filters support up to 15 and use assigned/active immutable rules rather than fabricating missing rows. Matrix one-point scores and Classic 1,500-point scores remain separate cohorts. Compatibility changes train no router and measure no new NLP accuracy; Render AI stays disabled until a secure separate connection preserves the local-only policy.

nodes.label: Private typed memory, social acts and fresh factual grounding
nodes.rationale: Whole-utterance curated social replies carry no metric claims and preserve validated context. Explicit new subjects override history. Staff-owned memory stores at most six typed contexts and language/detail preferences, never raw text or facts. Forget advances tombstone revision; memory failure cannot invent preferences or alter fresh analytics.

nodes.label: Explicit owner-reviewed routing examples and ambiguity
nodes.rationale: Collection requires explicit UI selection, separate human confirmation and current context/revision. Only current owner-approved sanitized examples can aid routing/export; stale/conflicting corrections require renewed review/clarification. Model has no training/review/export tools. External datasets and holdouts remain offline, and no automatic training/upload/activation occurs.

nodes.label: Backend factual response validation, bounded execution and outage fallback
nodes.rationale: V1 permits no model-written numeric claims. Fixed read-only repeatable-read queries and backend templates return scope/as_of/evidence/typed context. One 20-second deadline bounds auth/routing/analysis; metadata uses separate bounded best-effort background writes. Cold preparation is separate 120-second fixed-input calibration. Missing data is N/A; outages leave charts available.

nodes.label: Espressif NVS commit and error guarantees
nodes.rationale: Espressif NVS commit/error documentation motivates persist-before-receipt and retaining failed journals; it does not independently validate this firmware's flash behavior.

nodes.label: Espressif timer zero after deep sleep
nodes.rationale: Espressif documents monotonic timer reset after deep sleep; boot UUIDs scope clocks so uptime values from different boots are never compared as one timeline.

nodes.label: MariaDB transaction scoped FOR UPDATE locks
nodes.rationale: MariaDB row-lock behavior supports transaction-scoped serialization for recovery decisions; no transaction remains open across network I/O.

nodes.label: Boot-bound device recovery
nodes.rationale: Migration 005 extends original command delivery with current-boot authentication, immutable journals, terminal review and guarded operator recovery. Legacy mutation endpoints cannot bypass enrollment.

nodes.label: Historical local evidence: 305 backend, 23 recovery, 48 frontend and 9 Edge checks
nodes.rationale: Historical 20 November software evidence: full backend 305 passed; 23 recovery checks after retry fix and 306 collected distinct cases; 48 frontend tests/build, nine Edge flows, formatting/Ruff/document checks and local migration passed. Physical ESP32/NVS, power loss and phone/LAN were not run. Counts describe that milestone, not current summed coverage.

nodes.label: Accepted start terminal bindings and validated replay
nodes.rationale: Accepted/start/terminal evidence binds exact command, assigned rules and original boot/storage. Complete 12-level Classic or 15-level Matrix trace must satisfy deterministic and elapsed-time checks; missing-start/reboot terminal stays under review, while partial/changed/wrong-lineage evidence cannot earn points.

nodes.label: Conflicting evidence quarantines without force release
nodes.rationale: New storage epoch cannot prove never-started or recover old mismatched-epoch results. Contradictory authenticated evidence preserves originals and disables automatic resolution for investigation. No unrestricted force-release endpoint exists.

nodes.label: CSRF evidence revision reason and idempotency guarded decisions
nodes.rationale: Admin fence/resolve require CSRF, reason, revision and Idempotency-Key; resolution also binds evidence/action. Event→machine→session serialization commits ticket/command/result/notification/audit/receipt/live changes together. Exact retries reuse the saved response; changed key content fails; ready heartbeat is required after closure.

nodes.label: Current boot predecessor and persistent storage lineage
nodes.rationale: New boot registration persists exact boot/predecessor/storage/uptime first and supports exact retries. Retired boots cannot heartbeat/poll/start/result; new registration reviews active physical assignments, invalidates old evidence revisions and requires a fresh heartbeat.

nodes.label: Espressif timer reset and NVS commit motivate boot fencing
nodes.rationale: Boot-scoped clocks and durable commit requirements motivate evidence lineage, persist-before-receipt and retained failed journals. Filesystem emulator success cannot validate electrical brownout or flash guarantees.

nodes.label: Synthetic contract examples and mobile recovery overflow regression
nodes.rationale: Strict synthetic JSON examples show device/command/evidence bindings without credentials/identity. A 360px recovery assertion exposed wrapping overflow; the fix and four affected browser flows passed again, with screenshots inspected.

nodes.label: Permanent fence before guarded no score closure
nodes.rationale: Before a fence receipt, firmware must durably stop the session and persist a tombstone that rejects all old reserve/start commands across reboot/reconnect. Timeout, idle heartbeat and newly erased journals cannot attest never-started.

nodes.label: Unstarted release interrupted void and terminal recovery
nodes.rationale: Current-boot applied fence, matching evidence/revision and reason determine release-unstarted, explicit no-score interrupted void or full-trace replay recovery. Known terminal evidence cannot be discarded to release as unstarted; expired tickets rescan, recovered results notify exactly once.

nodes.label: Consecutive immutable journal receipts and scoped uptime
nodes.rationale: Journal event ID and consecutive per-boot sequence bind nondecreasing uptime, session/command/revision/phase. Exact replay returns original safe response even after resolution; conflicts persist quarantine instead of rolling it back with an error.

nodes.label: Version2 persistent emulator and unsent packet recovery
nodes.rationale: Separate v2 emulator persists boot/storage, exact unsent packets, start/terminal and permanent fences with flush/fsync/atomic replacement before send. Corrupt journals stop before networking; ordinary runs retry uncertain receipts, explicit reboot preserves lineage. CLI never assigns turns, presses a button or creates scores.

nodes.label: Version-bound terminal limits and recovery replay
nodes.rationale: Journal terminal schema allows up to 15 placements while replay enforces the assigned version: Classic 12, Matrix 15. Original boot/storage and immutable start marker remain mandatory. A complete trace can wait under review; invalid/partial/wrong-hash/wrong-lineage evidence cannot be promoted.

nodes.label: Post-resolution offline state and rescan requirement
nodes.rationale: Guarded recovery leaves cabinet offline until a new authenticated ready heartbeat. Ticket uniqueness permits one session only; expired players must scan again rather than recycle old tickets. This preserves original evidence and avoids silently granting another turn.

nodes.label: Device command delivery and review holds
nodes.rationale: Original v1 backend/emulator delivery contract is extended by boot-bound recovery. Current reserve/fence envelopes additionally expose monotonic deliverySequence; enrolled devices must use protocol-v2 journals.

nodes.label: Historical v1 checks extended by boot-bound recovery
nodes.rationale: Historical 19 November milestone ran 213 backend, 36 frontend, production build and synthetic Brave/axe checks. API/emulator recreation was checked then, not physical power cuts. The later v2 extension implements reconciliation/guarded release in software; old pending statements do not negate that extension, and hardware acceptance remains open.

nodes.label: Historical v1 persist-before-ACK and canonical retries
nodes.rationale: For never-enrolled legacy devices, read-only polls return own commands without consuming them. Persist command/session/revision/frozen rules before accepted/rejected ACK; canonical receipt deduplication and accepted-receipt start gating prevent duplicate transitions. Exact completed retries retain their original response.

nodes.label: Legacy command emulator does not prove NVS persistence
nodes.rationale: The separate v1 emulator polls/persists/ACKs only; it never registers/assigns/starts/scores/releases. Its ignored journal holds up to 32 command receipts, flushes and atomically replaces before resend, and rejects corruption before network. This is filesystem evidence, not ESP32 flash verification.

nodes.label: Review retains assigned ticket and active machine lock
nodes.rationale: Expired/rejected/staff-flagged assignments retain active cabinet uniqueness and assigned private tickets. A review flag blocks new starts/delivery but does not physically stop an already running game; idle/timeouts cannot prove non-start.

nodes.label: Monotonic delivery sequence and persistent rejection watermark
nodes.rationale: Reserve/fence envelopes expose database-monotonic deliverySequence; connected Matrix firmware persists the greatest accepted/stopped sequence before ACK and rejects all older reservations even after round detail changes. Database/device storage lineage must be preserved together or explicitly recovered; the value is ordering, not identity.

nodes.label: Safe command diagnostics and read-only AI boundary
nodes.rationale: Staff snapshots expose only last-five safe command metadata and labelled simulator state. Player live hints contain no command details. Acceptance is a device assertion, not proof of flash/hardware. AI gets no command/review authority; canonical hashes and private command contents stay private.

hyperedges.label: Constrained interpretation with fresh server-owned facts
Boot-scoped durable evidence and guarded resolution
